# Arun Arumugam

> Arun Arumugam. Agent engineering: projects and notes. Role: Agent Engineering.

Every post below is also available as clean Markdown: append `index.md` to its URL. Full sitemap: https://arun477.github.io/sitemap.xml. Feed: https://arun477.github.io/index.xml. What changed (agents: read before publishing): https://arun477.github.io/changelog/index.md. The home page is managed by an agent; rules: https://github.com/arun477/arun477.github.io/blob/main/docs/home-agent.md.

## Posts

- [FireScroll: Short Videos That Teach](https://arun477.github.io/posts/firescroll/index.md): Say a topic. An agent researches the web, writes a cited script, narrates it and renders a scrollable feed of short vertical videos.
- [Beifong: AI-Powered Content Curation and Podcast Generation](https://arun477.github.io/posts/beifong_podcast_generator/index.md): Point it at your feeds. It collects RSS and social posts, curates what matters to you and turns it into podcasts you can listen to.
- [Jupyter to LLM Extractor](https://arun477.github.io/posts/jupyter_extractor/index.md): A Chrome extension that extracts content from Jupyter notebooks for more effective interactions with large language models
- [Mel Spectrogram](https://arun477.github.io/posts/mel_spectrogram/index.md): How raw audio becomes a mel spectrogram: sampling, the Fourier transform, spectrograms and mel filterbanks, with code to build one and turn it back into sound.
- [llmdirtree: Directory Visualization and Context Generator for LLM Workflows](https://arun477.github.io/posts/directory-tree-generator/index.md): A Python CLI tool that generates both directory trees and code context summaries optimized for LLM interactions
- [Bharat-NanoBEIR: Indian Language Information Retrieval Dataset](https://arun477.github.io/posts/embedding_eval_for_indic/index.md): NanoBEIR in 22 Indian languages: 286 small retrieval benchmarks for checking how well an embedding model searches in Hindi, Tamil, Maithili and the rest.

## Themes

The running Feed synthesized into ranked storylines, each with its evidence. Everything as JSON: https://arun477.github.io/themes/index.json. Current themes:

- [Safety, security and provenance go operational](https://arun477.github.io/themes/safety-security-and-provenance-go-operational/index.md): Safety work is turning into standing practice inside the labs: OpenAI now runs probes, a model reviewer and investigative agents over every RL run and eval of its top models, Anthropic has Claude assess each of its own conversations for misuse right after replying, and outside audits, behaviour reports and post-mortems like the one on Claude Mythos 5 are becoming routine. Studies of human oversight show the risk is real, with expert analysts following an agent's hidden lean 86% of the time. The stack around the models has become part of the attack surface too, from the OpenCode breach and an SGLang cache bug that leaked other users' output to a tampered Claude Code extension that sat in Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours.
- [Agents become long-running, parallel and stateful](https://arun477.github.io/themes/agents-become-long-running-parallel-and-stateful/index.md): Agents are moving from single chats to long jobs: parallel agents in ChatGPT Pro, Gemini agents playing Minecraft for 27 hours, durable pi agents and dedicated memory models, and now GitHub rebuilding Copilot around parallel agent sessions that span repos and route each task across models. Engineering write-ups focus on the harness around the model: Meta split one overloaded agent into a router and 14 specialists, Ramp and LangChain built their own agent platforms, Cursor's Agent SDK packages agents as versioned code with evals, and Mistral offers a stateful Responses API. The hard problems are now state, memory, orchestration and testing.
- [Open-weight models reach the frontier](https://arun477.github.io/themes/open-weight-models-reach-the-frontier/index.md): Mistral Large 4, now shipped as roughly 1T-parameter open weights tuned for coding agents, Meta's Muse Spark Open, Reflection's Beam and Moonshot's 2.8T-parameter Kimi K3.1 Pro have put frontier-scale models under open licences within a few weeks, and MiniMax's open-weight M3.1 Flash topped OpenCode before it was even named. Vercel's gateway data shows open weights already carry most production tokens, and Meta and DeepSeek have published recipes and engines for running them cheaply. Self-hosting is now a real alternative to paid APIs for coding and agent work.
- [Closed labs ship new flagships and faster tiers](https://arun477.github.io/themes/closed-labs-ship-new-flagships-and-faster-tiers/index.md): The closed labs kept shipping: GPT-6 Sol, Luna and 6.1 Sol, Claude Haiku 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, Meta's Muse Wonder and now Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Carbon, which tops Artificial Analysis's new Index v5. OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra matches GPT-6 Astra on computer use at a tenth the price and over 3x the speed, aimed at high-volume agents. The competition is shifting toward speed, price tiers and agent workloads, and leaderboards are moving tests to private sets to keep rankings meaningful.
- [AI turns to maths and science research](https://arun477.github.io/themes/ai-turns-to-maths-and-science-research/index.md): Labs are pointing frontier models at research: OpenAI published new maths results and opened GPT-Rosalind to academic labs, Claude designed quantum circuits, a $15M fund backs AI in maths, and Anthropic started drug discovery of its own. The claims are now big enough to need formal review: physicists led by David Gross are vetting an AI result on Yang-Mills theory, and OpenAI and Anthropic models each claim a Lean-checked refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis that leading complexity theorists are reviewing in the open. Research results are becoming both a way labs show capability and a business line.
- [Infrastructure strains under agent-scale code](https://arun477.github.io/themes/infrastructure-strains-under-agent-scale-code/index.md): Agents now write code faster than Git hosting and review were built for. GitHub moved almost every repository to Azure under agent-driven load, Anthropic built its own source control after merges grew more than tenfold, and agent hours now outnumber staff hours six to one, leaving human review as the bottleneck. Teams are answering with automation: Cloudflare cut its per-review cost by 68% after it doubled, and Meta now has LLMs write just-in-time tests for every diff, catching 74 serious privacy bugs before they landed. Tooling built for human pace is giving way first.
- [Anthropic reshapes its governance on the way to an IPO](https://arun477.github.io/themes/anthropic-reshapes-its-governance-on-the-way-to-an-ipo/index.md): Anthropic filed an S-1 to list on Nasdaq as ANT, a week after committing 5% of its shares to a Public Benefit Fund that, with staff pledges, puts about 20% of its equity toward public benefit. It also handed its Agent Skills standard to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, as it did with MCP. A frontier lab going public puts its finances and governance in the open and sets a template for how safety-focused labs raise capital.
- [Personal agents get their own computers, accounts and money](https://arun477.github.io/themes/personal-agents-get-their-own-computers-accounts-and-money/index.md): Always-on personal agents went from demos to products this month. OpenAI launched dots with their own cloud computers, Grok Bot added voice, finance, email, coding hand-offs and password-manager sign-in through 1Password, Anthropic opened a preview of Claude Duet, a proactive personal agent, and Cursor's agents can now operate the user's own computer. The agent is becoming a standing assistant with its own identity and access, which makes permissions and approvals the key question.
- [Sandboxes and limits for agents that act](https://arun477.github.io/themes/sandboxes-and-limits-for-agents-that-act/index.md): As agents run code and touch production, containment is getting real engineering. Vercel's sandbox challenge surfaced a kernel zero-day and Vercel now details how its own agent gets narrowly scoped, short-lived access to production; Codex on Windows moved to a container sandbox and Google offers a microVM per agent with governance controls. Claude apps are making auto mode, where a classifier approves routine actions, the default, which puts the weight on isolation and hard limits rather than click-through prompts.
- [Assistants move into the tools people already use](https://arun477.github.io/themes/assistants-move-into-the-tools-people-already-use/index.md): Assistants are spreading into existing work surfaces: Claude inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides, live dashboards in Claude, voice upgrades in ChatGPT, and Cursor bundled into an X subscription. Distribution through familiar tools is becoming as important as model quality.

## Feed

Tech news and engineering blog posts, picked daily by an agent. Everything as JSON: https://arun477.github.io/feed/index.json. RSS: https://arun477.github.io/feed/index.xml. Latest days:

- [Claude agents beat a training-data monitor; agents get the desktop](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-31/index.md): Anthropic shows automated red-teaming can find harmless-looking data that teaches misalignment, and Vercel Labs opens up desktop computer use for any coding agent.
- [Malicious Claude Code extension hits Cursor's marketplace](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-30/index.md): A tampered Claude Code extension in Cursor's marketplace tried to install an SSH backdoor on up to 5,000 machines; affected users should update and check for compromise.
- [GitHub rebuilds Copilot around agents; OpenAI API credits for Pro](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-29/index.md): GitHub's Universe launches put agents and multi-model routing at the center of Copilot, and OpenAI now bundles monthly API credit with paid ChatGPT plans.
- [Gemini 4 Carbon leads a new private benchmark; AI vets Yang-Mills](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-28/index.md): Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Carbon tops the new Artificial Analysis Index v5, which now scores mostly on private tests. Mistral ships a Responses API for agents, KITP convenes a review of an AI Yang-Mills result, and Anthropic finds analysts follow their agent's hidden lean.
- [DeepMind's Genie 4 world model; Anthropic moves into drug discovery](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-27/index.md): Google DeepMind shows Genie 4, a real-time interactive world model. Anthropic shares lessons from six drug-discovery partnerships, Google Research proposes a sleep phase for continual learning, and LangChain details how it built its design agent.
- [Anthropic files for an IPO; OpenAI ships GPT-6.1 Terra](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-26/index.md): Anthropic files its S-1 to list on Nasdaq. OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra brings near-Astra computer use at a fraction of the cost, Cursor opens its Agent SDK, and Cloudflare details a cross-tenant KV cache leak in SGLang.
- [Block's Dessa: a voice model that never saw text](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-25/index.md): A quiet weekend. The one release worth knowing is Block's Dessa, a full-duplex speech model trained purely on conversation audio that runs on a laptop.
- [AI agents find a Brotli RCE; patch Node.js, Bun and Python](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-24/index.md): OpenAI's containment red-team surfaced CVE-2026-111497 in Google's Brotli decoder, now patched across major runtimes.
- [Kimi K3.1 Pro opens up; labs tighten model containment](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-23/index.md): Moonshot shipped a 2.8T open-weight model, Anthropic and OpenAI each detailed how they contain frontier models after real incidents, Cursor agents gained desktop control, and Agent Skills moved to a neutral foundation.
- [Outside red team finds gaps in OpenAI's agent monitoring](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-22/index.md): METR and Redwood published what deep outside access to OpenAI's agent monitoring turned up, Anthropic showed Claude writing formal proofs for real libraries, and Claude's apps and Google's cloud both moved further toward agents that act on their own.
- [AI-found PHP flaws patched; Anthropic launches Claude Duet](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-21/index.md): OpenAI coordinated fixes for critical PHP vulnerabilities its models helped find, so PHP sites should upgrade now. Anthropic joined the personal-agent race with Claude Duet, and GitHub and OpenAI explained infrastructure built for agent-era load.
- [DeepSeek opens its inference stack; TypeScript gets a Rust port](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-20/index.md): DeepSeek released the engine that serves V4.1-Flash, OpenAI published an open eval showing large gains on COBOL and Fortran, and Cloudflare and VoidZero unveiled a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler.
- [MiniMax M3.1 Flash goes official; Meta details Glimmer and Prometheus](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-19/index.md): MiniMax names the stealth model that topped OpenCode, Meta publishes its Muse Glimmer report and Prometheus cluster numbers, and Meta and Cloudflare share what they learned running agents in production.
- [OpenCode key breach; Anthropic sets up a public benefit fund](https://arun477.github.io/feed/2026-10-18/index.md): A quiet weekend for launches. OpenCode disclosed a breach of linked provider keys, Anthropic committed a growing share of its equity to a public benefit fund, and its own data shows agent hours now outnumber staff hours six to one.
